children: An update by AMP's China pension partner is seen by UBS as a timely reminder of the issues that come with such a linkup. While AMP's first-half profit from its 20% stake in China Life Pension Company more than doubled on a year earlier, analyst Kieren Chidgey notes that CLPC's latest solvency report highlights a flat third-quarter net profit. Chidgey tells clients this probably reflects weaker equity markets. He sees CLPC's long-term structural flow drivers as intact, but says the update highlights the asset's lower visibility relative to the Australian wealth manager's other operations. UBS maintains a neutral rating and trims its target price by 0.4% to 2.60 Australian dollars. Shares are down 6.8% at A$2.19. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
